title: Practice portal — notification copy
context: Content has approved the notification copy for the Notification Message page. The server picks one of the outcomes (success / failure) at random on each request; every message shown must be approved copy (story.md#L19, attachments/ux-copy.md).

sourcesRead.contributes: context and rule R1 (L19), AC-1 (L23), AC-2 (L24)
approved copy table (header L3; R2 values at L5-L6) and the close-icon rule (R3, L8)

acceptanceCriteria.quote: On the Notification Message page (`/notification_message_rendered`), each click on "Click here" shows exactly one notification, and its text is one of the approved messages in `ux-copy.md`.
acceptanceCriteria.text: On the Notification Message page (/notification_message_rendered), each click on "Click here" shows exactly one notification, and its text is one of the approved messages in ux-copy.md.
outcomes: each click on "Click here" shows exactly one notification
on every click, the notification text (close icon × excluded) is one of the approved messages: "Action successful" or "Action unsuccessful, please try again"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Across repeated clicks, both outcomes (success and failure) can occur.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Across repeated clicks, both outcomes (success and failure) can occur.
outcomes: across repeated clicks on "Click here", the success outcome ("Action successful") occurs at least once
across repeated clicks on "Click here", the failure outcome ("Action unsuccessful, please try again") occurs at least once

rules.text: The server picks one of the outcomes at random on each request, and every message shown must be approved copy.
Approved notification copy: Success → "Action successful"; Failure → "Action unsuccessful, please try again".
A close icon (×) may follow the message; it is not part of the copy.

testData.strategy: no data setup is stated in the sources and no AC needs pre-existing data: the server picks one of the outcomes at random on each request, so each click on "Click here" yields a fresh outcome

gaps.element: locator of the notification element and of its close icon on the Notification Message page

tried.result: L23 names the page route and the "Click here" link, but not how the notification is rendered
ux-copy.md#L8 says a close icon (×) may follow the message; no element names
inspect-01: getByRole('alert') matches 0; locator('#flash') matches 1 visible element; the close icon is a link named '×' inside it; 'Click here' is getByRole('link', { name: 'Click here' })

gaps.value: notification = locator('#flash') (one element); close icon = link '×' inside it, stripped before comparing text; trigger = getByRole('link', { name: 'Click here' })

gaps.element: how to wait for the outcome after each click

tried.result: L19: the server picks an outcome "on each request"; nothing on page behaviour
hardening: the page is reloaded on every click; each sample waits for DOMContentLoaded before reading the notification
the-internet profile notes: some pages load slow third-party assets, the load event can hang (so do not wait for 'load')

gaps.value: each click triggers a full page reload; wait for DOMContentLoaded (not the load event) before reading the notification

gaps.element: origin (base URL) of the application under test

tried.result: L23 gives only the route /notification_message_rendered; L9 is the Jira URL, not the app
evaluation.json aut = the-internet; heldout.config.json auts.the-internet.baseURL = https://the-internet.herokuapp.com (UI only)

gaps.element: how many clicks to sample for "each click" (AC-1) and "repeated clicks" (AC-2): the outcome is random and the story gives no number

tried.result: L19 "at random on each request"; L23 "each click"; L24 "across repeated clicks … can occur": no count, no probability
not asked: the extractor subagent cannot ask the user; to be confirmed by the evaluator

gaps.value: sample 12 clicks per test; AC-1 is checked on every one of the 12, AC-2 passes if each outcome appears at least once within the 12 (evaluator's sampling choice, not a requirement value)

gaps.element: how an outcome (success / failure) is recognised for AC-2, and whether a notification whose text matches no approved message counts as an occurrence of either outcome

tried.result: L24 names the outcomes "success and failure" but no signal that distinguishes them
ux-copy.md#L3-L6 pairs each outcome with exactly one message (Success → "Action successful", Failure → "Action unsuccessful, please try again"); it does not say how off-copy text should be classified
not asked: the extractor subagent cannot ask the user; to be confirmed by the evaluator

gaps.value: an outcome is recognised by its approved message from ux-copy.md: success = "Action successful", failure = "Action unsuccessful, please try again" (close icon × excluded); a notification matching neither message counts as neither outcome (it is an AC-1 failure)

coverage.note: also context: random outcome per request
approved copy table: L3 is the Outcome/Message header, L5 the Success row, L6 the Failure row (the values of R2)
